title.zh: 卷405 列傳一百九十二 曾国籓
title.raw: 卷405 列傳一百九十二 曾国籓

sentences.zh: 列傳一百九十二

translations.literal: Biographies 192
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 192

sentences.zh: 曾國籓

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan

sentences.zh: 曾國籓，初名子城，字滌生，湖南湘鄉人。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan, originally named Zicheng, courtesy name Disheng, was a native of Xiangxiang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan, born Zicheng and styled Disheng, came from Xiangxiang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 家世農。

translations.literal: His family for generations were farmers.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had been farmers.

sentences.zh: 祖玉屏，始慕鄉學。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuping first turned to village learning.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuping was the first in the line to take up scholarly study in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 父麟書，為縣學生，以孝聞。

translations.literal: His father Linshu was a county student, renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His father Linshu held county student status and was known for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 國籓，道光十八年進士。

translations.literal: Guofan passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan received his jinshi degree in the eighteenth year of the Daoguang reign.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以檢討典試四川，再轉侍讀，累遷內閣學士、禮部侍郎，署兵部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, as a reviser he conducted the provincial examination in Sichuan, then was transferred to reader-in-waiting, and was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat academician, Vice Minister of Rites, and acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he served as reviser and chief examiner in Sichuan, then became reader-in-waiting, and rose through Grand Secretariat academician and Vice Minister of Rites to acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 時太常寺卿唐鑑講學京師，國籓與倭仁、吳廷棟、何桂珍嚴事之，治義理之學。

translations.literal: At that time Tang Jian, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, lectured in the capital; Guofan together with Woren, Wu Tingdong, and He Guizhen served him with strict reverence and studied the learning of moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was then lecturing in the capital, and Guofan, together with Woren, Wu Tingdong, and He Guizhen, attended him devotedly and pursued the study of moral principle.

sentences.zh: 兼友梅曾亮及邵懿辰、劉傳瑩諸人，為詞章考據，尤留心天下人材。

translations.literal: He also befriended Mei Zengliang and Shao Yichen, Liu Chuanying, and others, engaging in belles-lettres and evidential scholarship, and paid special attention to talent throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He also kept company with Mei Zengliang, Shao Yichen, Liu Chuanying, and others in literary and evidential work, while keeping a keen eye on talent across the empire.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，廣西兵事起，詔群臣言得失。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign, military troubles arose in Guangxi, and the throne ordered the ministers to speak on gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign, fighting broke out in Guangxi, and the court called on the ministers to address what had gone right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 奏陳今日急務，首在用人，人才有轉移之道，有培養之方，有考察之法。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the urgent tasks of the day lay first in the use of men: talent had ways of being shifted, methods of cultivation, and means of inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial he argued that the day’s most pressing need was the proper use of men—that talent must be shifted, cultivated, and examined by deliberate methods.

sentences.zh: 上稱其剴切明辨。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his presentation as earnest, incisive, and clear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial as earnest, sharp, and clear.

sentences.zh: 尋疏薦李棠階、吳廷棟、王慶雲、嚴正基、江忠源五人。

translations.literal: Soon after he memorialized recommending five men: Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong, Wang Qingyun, Yan Zhengji, and Jiang Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed with a memorial recommending Li Tangjie, Wu Tingdong, Wang Qingyun, Yan Zhengji, and Jiang Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 寇氛益熾，复上言：「國用不足，兵伍不精，二者為天下大患。

translations.literal: As banditry grew fiercer, he again submitted: "State revenue is insufficient and the ranks are not well trained—these two are the great calamities of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebellion intensified, he wrote again: "Revenue is too thin and the troops are too slack—these are the empire’s gravest ills.

sentences.zh: 於歲入常額外，誠不可別求搜刮之術，增一分則民受一分之害。

translations.literal: Beyond the regular annual intake, one truly cannot seek separate schemes of squeezing and scraping; for every extra fraction levied, the people suffer a fraction’s harm.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond ordinary revenue there must be no new squeezing; every extra levy is an equal wound to the people.

sentences.zh: 至歲出之數，兵餉為鉅，綠營兵額六十四萬，常虛六七萬以資給軍用。

translations.literal: As to annual expenditure, military pay is the greatest item; the Green Standard rolls list six hundred forty thousand men, yet six or seven tens of thousands are habitually vacant to fund military use.
translations.idiomatic: Of yearly outlays, military pay is the largest; the Green Standard rolls claim six hundred forty thousand men, yet sixty or seventy thousand slots are routinely left empty to pad military funds.

sentences.zh: 自乾隆中增兵議起，歲糜帑二百餘萬。

translations.literal: From the mid-Qianlong debate on increasing troops, two million-odd taels were wasted yearly from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Since the mid-Qianlong push to enlarge the armies, more than two million taels a year have been drained from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 其時大學士阿桂即憂其難繼，嘉、道間兩次議裁，不及十之四，仍宜汰五萬，復舊額。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Secretary Agui already feared it could not be sustained; in the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns it was twice debated for reduction, yet not even four-tenths were cut; still five tens of thousands should be trimmed to restore the old quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Agui had already warned the burden could not last; under Jiaqing and Daoguang reductions were debated twice yet cut less than four-tenths—five tens of thousands should still be struck to restore the old rolls.

sentences.zh: 自古開國之初，兵少而國強，其後兵愈多則力愈弱，餉愈多則國愈貧。

translations.literal: Since antiquity at the founding of states, few troops meant a strong country; afterward the more troops, the weaker the force; the more pay, the poorer the state.
translations.idiomatic: At every dynasty’s founding, few soldiers meant a strong state; later, more soldiers meant weaker armies and more pay meant a poorer treasury.

sentences.zh: 應請皇上註意將才，但使七十一鎮中有十餘鎮足為心腹，則緩急可恃矣。

translations.literal: He asked the emperor to attend to commanders of talent: if but a dozen of the seventy-one garrisons were sound enough to serve as the heart and belly, then in crisis there would be something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to prize real commanders: if even a dozen of the seventy-one garrisons were trustworthy core forces, the court could count on them in an emergency.

sentences.zh: 」又深痛內外臣工諂諛欺飾，無陳善責難之風。

translations.literal: " He also deeply lamented that inner and outer officials flattered and deceived, without the spirit of presenting good counsel and holding one another to account.
translations.idiomatic: " He also lamented that court and province alike had sunk into flattery and concealment, with none of the old spirit of frank counsel and mutual reproof.

sentences.zh: 因上敬陳聖德預防流弊一疏，切指帝躬，有人所難言者，上優詔答之。

translations.literal: Therefore he submitted a memorial reverently setting forth sagely virtue and forestalling abuses, pointing directly at the emperor’s person with what others found hard to say; the emperor answered with an excellent edict.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore submitted a memorial on imperial virtue and the prevention of abuses, speaking bluntly to the throne where others would not; the emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 歷署刑部、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served in succession as acting Vice Minister of Justice and of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as acting Vice Minister of Justice and of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二年，典試江西，中途丁母憂歸。

translations.literal: In the second year he conducted examinations in Jiangxi, but midway mourned his mother and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed chief examiner in Jiangxi, but on the road he learned of his mother’s death and returned home in mourning.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵寇破江寧，據為偽都，分黨北犯河南、直隸，天下騷動，而國籓已前奉旨辦團練於長沙。

translations.literal: In the third year the Cantonese rebels took Jiangning and made it their false capital, sent parties north into Henan and Zhili, and the realm was in uproar, while Guofan had already earlier received orders to organize militia at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Taiping rebels seized Jiangning as their capital, sent columns north into Henan and Zhili, and threw the empire into turmoil—while Guofan had already been ordered to raise militia at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 初，國籓欲疏請終制，郭嵩燾曰：「公素具澄清之抱，今不乘時自效，如君父何？

translations.literal: At first Guofan wished to memorialize asking to complete mourning, but Guo Songtao said: "Your Excellency has long held the resolve to set things right; if you do not seize this moment to serve, what of your sovereign and father?
translations.idiomatic: At first Guofan meant to ask leave to finish mourning, but Guo Songtao said: "You have always wanted to set the realm right—if you will not act now, what becomes of your duty to sovereign and father?

sentences.zh: 且墨絰從戎，古制也。

translations.literal: Moreover, taking the field in mourning garb is an ancient institution.
translations.idiomatic: And taking the field in unbleached hemp is an ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 」遂不復辭。

translations.literal: " He then did not decline again.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he did not refuse again.

sentences.zh: 取明戚繼光遺法，募農民樸實壯健者，朝夕訓練之。

translations.literal: He took the surviving methods of the Ming general Qi Jiguang and recruited plain, sturdy farmers, training them morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Qi Jiguang’s methods from the Ming and recruited plain, sturdy peasants, drilling them from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 將領率用諸生，統眾數不逾五百，號「湘勇」。

translations.literal: Officers were drawn from degree-holders; each command did not exceed five hundred men, and they were called the "Xiang Braves."
translations.idiomatic: He put literati in command, kept units under five hundred men, and called them the Xiang Braves.

sentences.zh: 騰書遐邇，雖卑賤與鈞禮。

translations.literal: He sent letters far and wide and treated even the lowly with equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to men everywhere and treated even the humble as equals.

sentences.zh: 山野材智之士感其誠，莫不往見，人人皆以曾公可與言事。

translations.literal: Talented men of hill and wild, moved by his sincerity, all came to see him; everyone felt Lord Zeng was someone with whom affairs could be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Able men from the hills and countryside, stirred by his sincerity, came to call; all believed they could speak frankly with Lord Zeng.

sentences.zh: 四境土匪發，聞警即以湘勇往。

translations.literal: When bandits rose within the four borders, at the first alarm he sent the Xiang Braves.
translations.idiomatic: When local bandits flared up, he dispatched the Xiang Braves at the first report.

sentences.zh: 立三等法，不以煩府縣獄。

translations.literal: He established a three-grade law and did not trouble the prefectural and county prisons.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a three-tier code and kept cases out of the regular courts.

sentences.zh: 旬月中，莠民猾胥，便宜捕斬二百餘人。

translations.literal: Within a month or so, wicked commoners and crafty clerks—on convenient authority—were seized and beheaded, more than two hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he had seized and executed more than two hundred rogues and corrupt clerks on summary authority.

sentences.zh: 謗讟四起，自巡撫司道下皆心誹之，至以盛暑練操為虐士。

translations.literal: Slander rose on every side; from the governor and provincial intendant down, all inwardly resented him, even calling summer drill in the heat cruelty to the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Abuse spread everywhere; from the governor and intendants downward, officials seethed in private, some calling summer drill in the heat a torment to the men.

sentences.zh: 然見所奏輒得褒答受主知，未有以難也。

translations.literal: Yet when they saw his memorials they always won praise and favor from the sovereign, and none openly opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his memorials kept winning praise and imperial favor, and none dared openly stand in his way.

sentences.zh: 一日標兵與湘勇閧，至闌入國籓行台。

translations.literal: One day the garrison troops brawled with the Xiang Braves and even stormed into Guofan’s field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: One day the regular garrison fought the Xiang Braves and broke into Guofan’s headquarters.

sentences.zh: 國籓親訴諸巡撫，巡撫漫謝之，不為理，即日移營城外避標兵。

translations.literal: Guofan complained in person to the governor; the governor gave a perfunctory apology and would not act, so that very day he moved camp outside the walls to avoid the garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan appealed to the governor in person; the governor brushed him off and did nothing, so that day he moved his camp outside the city to escape the garrison.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「曷以聞？

translations.literal: Someone said: "Why not report it?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "Why not report this to the throne?

sentences.zh: 」國籓歎曰：「大難未已，吾人敢以私憤瀆君父乎？

translations.literal: " Guofan sighed: "The great calamity is not yet over—how dare we trouble the sovereign with private anger?
translations.idiomatic: " Guofan sighed: "The great crisis is not over—how dare we trouble the throne with a private quarrel?

sentences.zh: 嘗與嵩燾、忠源論東南形勢多阻水，欲勦賊非治水師不可，乃奏請造戰艦於衡州。

translations.literal: Once, discussing the southeast with Songtao and Zhongyuan, he said the terrain was full of waterways and rebels could not be suppressed without a navy; he memorialized to build warships at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Talking with Songtao and Zhongyuan about the southeast, he argued that waterways everywhere meant rebels could not be crushed without a fleet, and memorialized to build warships at Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 匠卒無曉船制者，短橈長槳，出自精思，以人力勝風水，遂成大小二百四十艦。

translations.literal: Craftsmen knew nothing of shipbuilding; with short oars and long paddles, born of careful thought, human strength overcame wind and water, and in the end two hundred forty large and small vessels were completed.
translations.idiomatic: No craftsman knew naval design; he devised short oars and long sweeps so muscle could beat wind and current, and two hundred forty vessels large and small were built.

sentences.zh: 募水陸萬人，水軍以褚汝航、楊載福、彭玉麟領之，陸軍以塔齊布、羅澤南領之。

translations.literal: He recruited ten thousand for land and water forces; the navy was led by Chu Ruhang, Yang Zaifu, and Peng Yulin, the army by Ta Qibu and Luo Zemin.
translations.idiomatic: He raised ten thousand men for land and river service: Chu Ruhang, Yang Zaifu, and Peng Yulin led the fleet; Ta Qibu and Luo Zemin the infantry.

sentences.zh: 賊自江西上竄，再陷九江、安慶。

translations.literal: The rebels from Jiangxi pushed upstream and again took Jiujiang and Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels moving up from Jiangxi retook Jiujiang and Anqing.

sentences.zh: 忠源戰歿廬州，吳文鎔督師黃州亦敗死。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan died in battle at Luzhou; Wu Wengong, commanding at Huangzhou, was also defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan fell at Luzhou; Wu Wengong, directing troops at Huangzhou, was defeated and killed as well.

sentences.zh: 漢陽失，武昌戒嚴，賊复乘勢擾湖南。

translations.literal: Hanyang was lost, Wuchang was placed on alert, and the rebels again took advantage to harass Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Hanyang fell, Wuchang was put on alert, and the rebels again raided Hunan.

sentences.zh: 國籓銳欲討賊，率水陸軍東下。

translations.literal: Guofan was keen to attack the rebels and led land and naval forces east.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan was eager to strike and led his combined force eastward.

sentences.zh: 舟師初出湖，大風，損數十艘。

translations.literal: When the fleet first left the lake, a great wind wrecked several tens of vessels.
translations.idiomatic: As the fleet first cleared the lake, a gale destroyed dozens of boats.

sentences.zh: 陸師至岳州，前隊潰退，引還長沙。

translations.literal: The army reached Yuezhou, the vanguard was routed and fell back, and they withdrew to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Yuezhou, its van was broken and driven back to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 賊陷湘潭，邀擊靖港，又敗，國籓憤投水，幕下士章壽麟掖起之，得不死。

translations.literal: The rebels took Xiangtan and intercepted at Jinggang; defeated again, Guofan in rage threw himself into the water, and his staff member Zhang Shoulin pulled him up so that he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels seized Xiangtan and beat him again at Jinggang; in despair Guofan threw himself into the river, and Zhang Shoulin of his staff hauled him out alive.

sentences.zh: 而同時塔齊布大破賊湘潭，國籓營長沙高峰寺，重整軍實，人人捓揄之。

translations.literal: Yet at the same time Ta Qibu routed the rebels at Xiangtan; Guofan camped at Gaofeng Temple in Changsha, reorganized the army, and everyone mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the same moment Ta Qibu smashed the rebels at Xiangtan; Guofan camped at Gaofeng Temple in Changsha to rebuild his force while men jeered at him.

sentences.zh: 或請增兵，國籓曰：「吾水陸萬人非不多，而遇賊即潰。

translations.literal: Some asked to increase the troops; Guofan said: "My land and water force of ten thousand is not small, yet at every encounter with rebels they collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged more troops; Guofan said: "Ten thousand men on land and water are not few, yet we break whenever we meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 岳州之敗，水師拒戰者惟載福一營；

translations.literal: At the defeat at Yuezhou, of the navy only Zaifu’s one battalion stood and fought;
translations.idiomatic: At Yuezhou only Zaifu’s single battalion in the fleet stood firm;

sentences.zh: 湘潭之戰，陸師塔齊布、水師載福各兩營：以此知兵貴精不貴多。

translations.literal: at the battle of Xiangtan, on land Ta Qibu and on water Zaifu each had two battalions: from this one knows troops value quality, not quantity.
translations.idiomatic: at Xiangtan Ta Qibu had two infantry battalions and Zaifu two on the river—that shows quality, not numbers, wins wars.

sentences.zh: 故諸葛敗祁山，且謀減兵損食，勤求己過，非虛言也。

translations.literal: Thus when Zhuge failed at Qishan he still planned to reduce troops and cut rations, diligently seeking his own faults—it was no empty phrase.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Liang failed at Qishan he still meant to cut men and rations and examine his own faults—that was no idle saying.

sentences.zh: 且古人用兵，先明功罪賞罰。

translations.literal: Moreover, in ancient warfare one first made clear merit, guilt, reward, and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: And in antiquity one first fixed merit, fault, reward, and punishment.

sentences.zh: 今世亂，賢人君子皆潛伏，吾以義聲倡導，同履危亡。

translations.literal: In today’s disorder, worthy gentlemen all lie hidden; I raise the banner of righteousness and share danger with them.
translations.idiomatic: In today’s chaos worthy men lie low; I call them out by righteousness and share their peril.

sentences.zh: 諸公之初從我，非以利動也，故於法亦有難施，其致敗由此。

translations.literal: When you first followed me, it was not profit that moved you, so the law is hard to apply strictly—defeat comes from this.
translations.idiomatic: You joined me not for gain, so strict law is hard—and that is why we lose.

sentences.zh: 」諸將聞之皆服。

translations.literal: " The generals hearing this all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " The commanders, hearing this, were convinced.

sentences.zh: 陸師既克湘潭，巡撫、提督上功，而國籓請罪。

translations.literal: Once the army had taken Xiangtan, the governor and provincial military commissioner reported merit, while Guofan asked to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiangtan fell, the governor and commander reported victory while Guofan asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 上詰責提督鮑起豹，免其官，以塔齊布代之。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Military Commissioner Bao Qibao, removed him from office, and replaced him with Ta Qibu.
translations.idiomatic: The throne rebuked Bao Qibao and removed him, putting Ta Qibu in his place.

sentences.zh: 受印日，士民聚觀，嘆詫國籓為知人，而天子能明見萬里也。

translations.literal: On the day he received the seal, officials and people gathered to watch and marveled that Guofan knew men and that the Son of Heaven could see ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: When Ta Qibu took command, crowds gathered in wonder that Guofan knew men and that the emperor saw clear across the realm.

sentences.zh: 賊自岳州陷常德，旋北走，武昌再失。

translations.literal: The rebels from Yuezhou took Changde, then turned north; Wuchang was lost again.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Yuezhou seized Changde, swept north, and Wuchang fell again.

sentences.zh: 國籓引兵趨岳州，斬賊梟將曾天養，連戰，下城陵磯。

translations.literal: Guofan led troops toward Yuezhou, beheaded the rebel chieftain Zeng Tianyang, fought repeatedly, and took Chenglingji.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan marched on Yuezhou, beheaded the rebel leader Zeng Tianyang, fought on, and took Chenglingji.

sentences.zh: 會師金口，謀取武昌。

translations.literal: He joined forces at Jinkou and planned to take Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Forces gathered at Jinkou to retake Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 澤南沿江東岸攻花園寇屯，塔齊布伏兵洪山，載福舟師深入寇屯，士皆露立，不避鉛丸。

translations.literal: Zemin attacked rebel stockades along the east bank at Huayuan; Ta Qibu lay in ambush at Hongshan; Zaifu’s fleet drove deep into rebel positions, and the men stood exposed, not dodging shot.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zemin struck rebel camps on the east bank at Huayuan; Ta Qibu hid at Hongshan; Zaifu’s boats drove into enemy lines while his men stood in the open, ignoring musket fire.

sentences.zh: 武昌、漢陽賊望見官軍盛，宵遁，遂復二郡。

translations.literal: Rebels in Wuchang and Hanyang, seeing the government army’s strength, fled by night, and the two prefectures were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the government host, the garrisons at Wuchang and Hanyang fled by night and both cities were recovered.

sentences.zh: 國籓以前靖港敗，自請奪官，至是奏上，詔署湖北巡撫，尋加兵部侍郎銜，解署任，命督師東下。

translations.literal: Guofan, for his earlier defeat at Jinggang, had asked that his rank be stripped; now he reported upward, and was ordered to act as Governor of Hubei, soon given the rank of Vice Minister of War, released from the acting governorship, and commanded to lead the army east.
translations.idiomatic: He had asked to be stripped of rank after Jinggang; now the court made him acting governor of Hubei, soon Vice Minister of War, relieved of the governorship, and ordered east at the head of the army.

sentences.zh: 當是時，水師奮厲無前，大破賊田家鎮，斃賊數万，至於九江，前鋒薄湖口。

translations.literal: At that time the navy pressed forward without pause, routed the rebels at Tianjiazhen, killed tens of thousands, reached Jiujiang, and the vanguard closed on Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet then drove forward, shattered the rebels at Tianjiazhen, killed tens of thousands, reached Jiujiang, and the van pressed Hukou.

sentences.zh: 攻梅家洲賊壘不下，駛入鄱湖。

translations.literal: They could not take the rebel fort at Meijiazhou and sailed into Poyang Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Failing at Meijiazhou, they entered Poyang Lake.

sentences.zh: 賊築壘湖口斷其後，舟不得出，於是外江、內湖阻絕。

translations.literal: Rebels built fortifications at Hukou to cut them off behind; the boats could not get out, and the outer river and inner lake were severed.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels walled Hukou behind them; trapped, the outer Yangtze and inner lake were cut off from each other.

sentences.zh: 外江戰船無小艇，賊乘舴艋夜襲營，擲火燒坐船，​​國籓跳而免，水師遂大亂。

translations.literal: On the outer river the warships had no small boats; rebels in skiffs raided the camp by night, threw fire onto the command vessels, and Guofan leaped clear; the navy fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The great ships had no tenders; rebels in light craft burned the flagships by night and Guofan leaped clear while the fleet collapsed.

sentences.zh: 上疏請罪，詔旨寬免，謂於大局無傷也。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking punishment; the edict was lenient, saying the overall situation was not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be punished; the edict was mild, saying the larger cause was unhurt.

sentences.zh: 五年，賊再陷武漢，擾荊襄。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the rebels again took Wuhan and harassed Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the rebels retook Wuhan and raided Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 國籓遣胡林翼等軍還援湖北，塔齊布留攻九江，而躬至南昌撫定水師之困內湖者。

translations.literal: Guofan sent Hu Linyi and others back to aid Hubei, left Ta Qibu to besiege Jiujiang, and went in person to Nanchang to steady the fleet trapped in the inner lake.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Hu Linyi to relieve Hubei, left Ta Qibu at Jiujiang, and went to Nanchang to steady the fleet trapped inland.

sentences.zh: 澤南從征江西，复弋陽，拔廣信，破義寧，而塔齊布卒於軍。

translations.literal: Zemin campaigned in Jiangxi, retook Yiyang, took Guangxin, broke Yining, and Ta Qibu died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zemin fought through Jiangxi, retook Yiyang and Guangxin, broke Yining, and Ta Qibu died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 國籓在江西與巡撫陳啟邁不相能，澤南奔命往來，上書國籓，言東南大勢在武昌，請率所部援鄂，國籓從之。

translations.literal: Guofan in Jiangxi could not work with Governor Chen Qimai; Zemin rushed back and forth on orders, wrote to Guofan that the great trend of the southeast lay at Wuchang, and asked to lead his troops to aid Hubei; Guofan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi he clashed with Governor Chen Qimai; Luo Zemin shuttled between fronts, wrote that the southeast turned on Wuchang, and begged to march to Hubei—Guofan consented.

sentences.zh: 幕客劉蓉諫曰：「公所恃者塔、羅。

translations.literal: Staff member Liu Rong remonstrated: "What Your Excellency relies on are Ta and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rong warned him: "You depend on Ta and Luo.

sentences.zh: 今塔將軍亡，羅又遠行，脫有急，誰堪使者？

translations.literal: Now General Ta is dead and Luo has gone far—if trouble comes, who can be sent?
translations.idiomatic: Ta is dead and Luo is far away—if crisis strikes, whom will you send?

sentences.zh: 」國籓曰：「吾計之熟矣，東南大局宜如是，俱困於此無為也。

translations.literal: " Guofan said: "I have thought it through; the great pattern of the southeast should be so—both stuck here accomplishes nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " Guofan said: "I have weighed it: the southeast must be served this way—staying here helps nothing.

sentences.zh: 」嵩燾祖餞澤南曰：「曾公兵單，奈何？

translations.literal: " Songtao, seeing Zemin off, said: "Lord Zeng’s force is thin—what then?
translations.idiomatic: " At Zemin’s farewell Songtao asked: "Lord Zeng’s troops are few—what then?

sentences.zh: 」澤南曰：「天苟不亡本朝，公必不死。

translations.literal: " Zemin said: "If Heaven does not wish this dynasty destroyed, he will not die.
translations.idiomatic: " Zemin answered: "If Heaven means to keep the dynasty, he will not die.

sentences.zh: 」九月，補授兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month he was formally appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth month he received formal appointment as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊酋石達開由湖北竄江西，連陷八府一州，九江賊踞自如，湖南北聲息不相聞。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the rebel chief Shi Dakai from Hubei fled into Jiangxi, seized eight prefectures and one subprefecture in succession, rebels at Jiujiang held firm as before, and north and south Hunan could not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Shi Dakai fled from Hubei into Jiangxi and swept eight prefectures and one department; Jiujiang rebels held on, and Hunan north and south lost touch.

sentences.zh: 國籓困南昌，遣將分屯要地，羽檄交馳，不廢吟誦。

translations.literal: Guofan, besieged at Nanchang, sent generals to garrison key points; urgent dispatches flew, yet he did not cease recitation.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged at Nanchang, he posted generals at key points, dispatch piled on dispatch, yet he still recited his texts.

sentences.zh: 作水陸師得勝歌，教軍士戰守技藝、結營布陳之法，歌者咸感奮，以殺賊敢死為榮。

translations.literal: He composed songs of victory for land and water forces, teaching the troops fighting and guarding skills and methods of camp and array; those who sang were all stirred and took dying to kill rebels as glory.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote victory songs for army and fleet, drilling men in tactics and encampment; singers were roused to glory in killing rebels at the risk of death.

sentences.zh: 顧眾寡，終不能大挫賊。

translations.literal: Yet considering numbers, in the end he could not inflict a great blow on the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: But given his numbers, he still could not break the enemy decisively.

sentences.zh: 議者爭請調澤南軍，上以武漢功垂成，不可棄。

translations.literal: Critics all asked to transfer Zemin’s army; the emperor, because Wuhan was near success, would not abandon it.
translations.idiomatic: Critics demanded Luo Zemin’s troops; the throne, seeing Wuhan almost won, refused.

sentences.zh: 澤南督戰益急，卒死於軍。

translations.literal: Zemin pressed the fighting ever harder and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zemin drove the fighting harder still and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 玉麟聞江西警，芒鞋走千里，穿賊中至南昌助守。

translations.literal: Yulin, hearing of the Jiangxi alarm, walked a thousand li in straw sandals through rebel lines to Nanchang to help defend.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yulin, hearing of Jiangxi’s peril, walked a thousand li in sandals through rebel country to help hold Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 林翼已為湖北巡撫，國籓弟國華、國葆用父命乞師林翼，將五千人攻瑞州。

translations.literal: Linyi was already Governor of Hubei; Guofan’s brothers Guohua and Guobao, by their father’s order, begged troops from Linyi and led five thousand to attack Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi was now governor of Hubei; brothers Guohua and Guobao, by their father’s command, borrowed five thousand men from Linyi and attacked Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 湖南巡撫駱秉章亦資國荃兵援吉安，兄弟皆會行間。

translations.literal: Hunan Governor Luo Bingzhang also supplied Guoquan’s troops to aid Ji’an, and the brothers all met in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan’s Luo Bingzhang sent Guoquan to Ji’an, and the brothers joined in the field.

sentences.zh: 而國籓前所遣援湖北諸軍，久之再克武漢，直下九江，李續賓八千人軍城東。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the forces Guofan had earlier sent to aid Hubei, after long fighting, retook Wuhan and drove straight to Jiujiang, where Li Xubin with eight thousand men camped east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile his earlier Hubei relief force, after long fighting, retook Wuhan, pushed to Jiujiang, and Li Xubin encamped east of the city with eight thousand.

sentences.zh: 續賓者，與弟續宜皆澤南高第弟子也。

translations.literal: Xubin and his brother Xuyi were both leading disciples of Zemin.
translations.idiomatic: Xubin and his brother Xuyi were both foremost pupils of Luo Zemin.

sentences.zh: 載福戰船四百泊江兩岸，江寧將軍都興阿馬隊、鮑超步隊駐小池口，凡數万人。

translations.literal: Zaifu’s four hundred war junks lay on both banks; Jiangning General Duxing’a’s cavalry and Bao Chao’s infantry were at Xiaochikou—tens of thousands in all.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred of Zaifu’s war boats lined the banks; Duxing’a’s Manchu horse and Bao Chao’s foot held Xiaochikou—tens of thousands altogether.

sentences.zh: 國籓本以憂懼治軍，自南昌迎勞，見軍容甚盛，益申儆告誡之。

translations.literal: Guofan had governed the army in anxiety; meeting them at Nanchang on their return, he saw the host’s strength and redoubled stern warnings.
translations.idiomatic: He had led in worry; meeting them at Nanchang he saw their strength and preached caution all the harder.

sentences.zh: 而是時江南大營潰，督師向榮退守丹陽，卒。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the great Jiangnan camp collapsed; Commander Xiang Rong fell back to Danyang and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yet then the great Jiangnan camp collapsed; Commander-in-chief Xiang Rong fell back to Danyang and died.

sentences.zh: 和春為欽差大臣，張國樑總統諸軍攻江寧。

translations.literal: He Chun served as Imperial Commissioner, and Zhang Guoliang as overall commander of the armies attacking Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun was named Imperial Commissioner and Zhang Guoliang supreme commander of the forces against Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，國籓聞父憂，迳歸。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, Guofan heard of his father’s death and returned straightway.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year he learned of his father’s death and went home at once.

sentences.zh: 給三月假治喪，堅請終制，允開侍郎缺。

translations.literal: He was granted three months’ leave for mourning and firmly asked to complete mourning; he was allowed to vacate his vice-ministerial post.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave him three months to mourn and he begged to observe full mourning; he was permitted to leave his vice-ministerial post open.

sentences.zh: 林翼既定湖北，進圍九江，破湖口，水師絕數年復合。

translations.literal: Linyi had already secured Hubei and pressed the siege of Jiujiang, took Hukou, and after several years the navy was reunited.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi had pacified Hubei, besieged Jiujiang, retook Hukou, and after years the fleet was whole again.

sentences.zh: 載福連拔望江、東流，揚風過安慶，克銅陵泥汊，與江南軍通。

translations.literal: Zaifu took Wangjiang and Dongliu in succession, sailed past Anqing, took Tongling and Nizha, and linked with the Jiangnan army.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zaifu swept Wangjiang and Dongliu, passed Anqing, seized Tongling and Nizha, and joined the Jiangnan forces.

sentences.zh: 由是湘軍水師名天下。

translations.literal: From this the Xiang Army navy was famed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiang Army’s river force became famous empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 林翼以此軍創始國籓，楊、彭皆其舊部，請起國籓視師。

translations.literal: Linyi, because this army was founded by Guofan and Yang and Peng were his old subordinates, asked that Guofan be recalled to command.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi, knowing the fleet was Guofan’s creation and that Yang and Peng were his men, asked the throne to recall Guofan to take command.

sentences.zh: 會九江克復，石達開竄浙江，浸及福建，分股复犯江西，朝旨詔國籓出辦浙江軍務。

translations.literal: When Jiujiang was recovered, Shi Dakai fled to Zhejiang and gradually reached Fujian; detachments again invaded Jiangxi, and an imperial order summoned Guofan to manage Zhejiang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang fell, Shi Dakai fled toward Zhejiang and Fujian, rebel columns re-entered Jiangxi, and Guofan was ordered to take charge of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 國籓至江西，屯建昌，又詔援閩。

translations.literal: Guofan reached Jiangxi and encamped at Jianchang; he was again ordered to aid Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Jiangxi and camped at Jianchang, then was ordered to relieve Fujian as well.

sentences.zh: 國籓以閩賊不足慮，而景德地衝要，遣將援贛北，攻景德。

translations.literal: Guofan held that Fujian rebels were not worth worry, but Jingde was strategically vital; he sent generals to aid northern Gan and attack Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: He judged Fujian a lesser threat but Jingde vital, and sent troops to aid northern Jiangxi and strike Jingde.

sentences.zh: 國荃追賊至浮梁，江西列城次第复。

translations.literal: Guoquan pursued rebels to Fuliang, and Jiangxi’s walled cities were recovered one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan drove the enemy to Fuliang, and Jiangxi’s cities fell back in order.

sentences.zh: 時石達開復竄湖南，圍寶慶。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Dakai again fled into Hunan and besieged Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai then turned back into Hunan and besieged Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 上慮四川且有變，林翼亦以湖北餉倚川鹽，而國籓又久治兵，無疆寄，乃與官文合疏請國籓援蜀。

translations.literal: The emperor feared Sichuan might also change; Linyi too relied on Sichuan salt for Hubei’s supplies, and Guofan had long commanded troops without a frontier post; thus together with Guan Wen they memorialized asking Guofan to aid Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared trouble in Sichuan; Linyi’s revenue depended on Sichuan salt, and Guofan had no provincial post—he and Guan Wen jointly asked that he march to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 會賊竄廣西，上游兵事解，而陳玉成再破廬州，續賓戰歿三河，林翼以群盜蔓廬、壽間，終為楚患，乃改議留國籓合謀皖。

translations.literal: Then rebels fled into Guangxi, upstream fighting eased, but Chen Yucheng again took Luzhou and Xubin died at Sanhe; Linyi, seeing bandits spread between Luzhou and Shouzhou, a lasting menace to Chu, changed plan and kept Guofan to join in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels then fled to Guangxi and the upper river quieted, but Chen Yucheng retook Luzhou and Li Xubin died at Sanhe; Linyi, seeing bandits between Luzhou and Shouzhou, kept Guofan for the Anhui campaign instead.

sentences.zh: 軍分三道，各萬人。

translations.literal: The army was divided into three columns, each ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Three columns of ten thousand men each were formed.

sentences.zh: 國籓由宿松、石牌規安慶，多隆阿、鮑超出太湖取桐城，林翼自英山鄉舒、六。

translations.literal: Guofan from Susong and Shipai aimed at Anqing; Duo Long’a and Bao Chao from Taihu took Tongcheng; Linyi from Yingshan toward Shu and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan advanced from Susong and Shipai on Anqing; Duo Long’a and Bao Chao from Taihu on Tongcheng; Hu Linyi from Yingshan on Shuzhou and Liuan.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿等既大破賊小池，复太湖、潛山，遂軍桐城。

translations.literal: Duo Long’a and others, having routed rebels at Xiaochi, recovered Taihu and Qianshan, then encamped at Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Duo Long’a smashed the enemy at Xiaochi, retook Taihu and Qianshan, and encamped at Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 國荃率諸軍圍安慶，與桐城軍相犄角。

translations.literal: Guoquan led the armies to besiege Anqing, pincering with the Tongcheng force.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan besieged Anqing while the Tongcheng army held the other horn.

sentences.zh: 安慶未及下，而皖南賊陷廣德，襲破杭州。

translations.literal: Before Anqing fell, southern Anhui rebels took Guangde and stormed Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Anqing was still untaken when rebels in southern Anhui seized Guangde and broke Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 李秀成大會群賊建平，分道援江寧，江南大營复潰，常州、蘇州相繼失，咸豐十年閏三月也。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng gathered rebels at Jianping, sent columns to relieve Jiangning, the great Jiangnan camp collapsed again, and Changzhou and Suzhou fell in succession—it was the intercalary third month of the tenth year of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng massed at Jianping, sent relief to Jiangning, the Jiangnan camp collapsed again, and Changzhou and Suzhou fell—it was the intercalary third month, tenth year of Xianfeng.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠聞而歎曰：「此勝敗之轉機也！

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang heard and sighed: "This is the turning point of victory and defeat!
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang sighed: "Here is the turning point of the war!

sentences.zh: 江南諸軍，將蹇兵疲久矣。

translations.literal: The armies of Jiangnan have long had failing generals and weary troops.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan’s armies have had bad commanders and exhausted men for years.

sentences.zh: 滌而清之，庶幾後來可藉手乎？

translations.literal: Wash and clear them—perhaps later one may have something to work with?
translations.idiomatic: Wash them clean—perhaps we can use them again?

sentences.zh: 」或問：「誰可當者？

translations.literal: " Someone asked: "Who can take charge?
translations.idiomatic: " Someone asked: "Who is fit to lead?

sentences.zh: 」林翼曰：「朝廷以江南事付曾公，天下不足平也。

translations.literal: " Linyi said: "If the court entrusts Jiangnan to Lord Zeng, the realm is not beyond pacification.
translations.idiomatic: " Linyi said: "Put Jiangnan in Lord Zeng’s hands and the empire can be settled.

sentences.zh: 」於是天子慎選帥，就加國籓兵部尚書銜，署理兩江總督，旋即真，授欽差大臣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Son of Heaven carefully chose a commander, promoted Guofan to Minister of War rank, made him acting Governor-General of the Two Jiangs, soon confirmed, and appointed Imperial Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then raised Guofan to Minister of War, made him acting governor-general of the Two Jiangs, confirmed him, and named him Imperial Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時江、浙賊氛熾，或請撤安慶圍先所急。

translations.literal: At that time rebel flames in Jiangsu and Zhejiang were fierce; some asked to lift the Anqing siege for more urgent needs.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels blazed in Jiangsu and Zhejiang; some urged lifting the siege of Anqing for the crisis elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 國籓曰：「安慶一軍為克金陵張本，不可動也。

translations.literal: Guofan said: "The Anqing army is the foundation for taking Jinling; it cannot be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan replied: "The force at Anqing is the key to Nanjing; it must not move.

sentences.zh: 」遂南渡江，駐祁門。

translations.literal: " He then crossed the Yangtze south and encamped at Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: " He crossed the river and camped at Qimen.

sentences.zh: 江、浙官紳告急書日數十至，援蘇、援滬、援皖、援鎮江詔書亦疊下。

translations.literal: Urgent letters from Jiangsu and Zhejiang officials arrived by the dozen daily; edicts to relieve Suzhou, Shanghai, Anhui, and Zhenjiang also piled up.
translations.idiomatic: Daily pleas poured in from Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and edicts to save Suzhou, Shanghai, Anhui, and Zhenjiang followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 國籓至祁門未數日，賊陷寧國，陷徽州。

translations.literal: Within days of reaching Qimen, rebels took Ningguo and Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Days after he reached Qimen, Ningguo and Huizhou fell.

sentences.zh: 東南方困兵革，而英吉利复失好，以兵至。

translations.literal: The southeast was worn by war, and England again broke relations and came with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast was ravaged by war, and Britain, relations broken, sent troops.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁敗績天津，文宗狩熱河，國籓聞警，請提兵北上，會和議成，乃止。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen was defeated at Tianjin; Emperor Wenzong hunted at Rehe; Guofan, hearing the alarm, asked to lead troops north, but peace was made and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen was beaten at Tianjin and Emperor Wenzong fled to Rehe; Guofan offered to march north, but peace was made and he held back.

sentences.zh: 其冬，大為賊困，一出祁門東陷婺源；

translations.literal: That winter he was greatly beset by rebels: one column east from Qimen took Wuyuan;
translations.idiomatic: That winter rebels hemmed him in on three sides: one force east from Qimen took Wuyuan;

sentences.zh: 一出祁門西陷景德；

translations.literal: one west from Qimen took Jingde;
translations.idiomatic: one west from Qimen retook Jingde;

sentences.zh: 一入羊棧嶺攻大營。

translations.literal: one entered Yangzhan Ridge and attacked the great camp.
translations.idiomatic: one came through Yangzhan Ridge against headquarters.

sentences.zh: 軍報絕不通，將吏惵然有憂色，固請移營江乾就水師。

translations.literal: Military reports could not get through; officers and men looked fearful and firmly asked to move camp to the riverbank to join the navy.
translations.idiomatic: Couriers could not pass; officers begged to move to the river and the fleet.

sentences.zh: 國籓曰：「無故退軍，兵家所忌。

translations.literal: Guofan said: "To retreat without cause is what strategists forbid.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan said: "A retreat without cause is forbidden in war.

sentences.zh: 」卒不從，使人間行檄鮑超、張運蘭亟引兵會。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not agree, but sent men by secret paths to summon Bao Chao and Zhang Yunlan to hurry with their troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He refused, but sent secret orders for Bao Chao and Zhang Yunlan to march at once.

sentences.zh: 身在軍中，意氣自如，時與賓佐酌酒論文。

translations.literal: Though in the army, his spirit was as calm as ever; he sometimes drank and discussed literature with his staff.
translations.idiomatic: In camp his bearing stayed calm; he still drank and talked letters with his advisers.

sentences.zh: 自官京朝，即日記所言行，後履危困無稍間。

translations.literal: From his days in the capital he had daily recorded words and deeds, and later amid peril he never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Since his Beijing days he had kept a daily journal, and in danger he never stopped.

sentences.zh: 國籓駐祁門，本資餉江西，及景德失，議者爭言取徽州通浙米。

translations.literal: Guofan at Qimen had relied on Jiangxi for supplies; when Jingde fell, critics all said take Huizhou to open Zhejiang grain.
translations.idiomatic: At Qimen he had lived on Jiangxi supplies; after Jingde fell, many said seize Huizhou for Zhejiang rice.

sentences.zh: 乃自將大軍次休寧，值天雨，八營皆潰，草遺囑寄家，誓死守休寧。

translations.literal: He led the main army to Xiuning; rain came, eight camps were routed, he drafted a will for his family, and swore to die defending Xiuning.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Xiuning; rain broke eight camps; he wrote his will home and swore to hold Xiuning or die.

sentences.zh: 適宗棠大破賊樂平，運道通，移駐東流。

translations.literal: Just then Zongtang routed rebels at Leping, the supply route opened, and he moved camp to Dongliu.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang then smashed the enemy at Leping, supplies returned, and he shifted to Dongliu.

sentences.zh: 多隆阿連敗賊桐城，鮑超一軍游擊無定居，林翼復遣將助之。

translations.literal: Duo Long’a repeatedly defeated rebels at Tongcheng; Bao Chao’s column ranged without fixed base; Linyi again sent generals to help.
translations.idiomatic: Duo Long’a beat the enemy at Tongcheng again; Bao Chao ranged freely; Hu Linyi sent more help.

sentences.zh: 十一年八月，國荃遂克安慶。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eleventh year Guoquan finally took Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eleventh year Guoquan took Anqing.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，而文宗崩，林翼亦卒。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, Emperor Wenzong died and Linyi also died.
translations.idiomatic: News of victory came as Emperor Wenzong died—and Hu Linyi with him.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，太后垂簾聽政，加國籓太子少保銜，命節制江蘇、安徽、江西、浙江四省。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong succeeded; the empress dowager ruled from behind the curtain; Guofan was given Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent rank and ordered to control Jiangsu, Anhui, Jiangxi, and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong reigned under the empress dowager’s regency; Guofan became Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and commander of four provinces.

sentences.zh: 國籓惶懼，疏辭，不允，朝有大政，諮而後行。

translations.literal: Guofan was fearful and declined in a memorial, but was not allowed; on great court policy he was consulted before action.
translations.idiomatic: He begged off in fear; the court refused; major policy waited on his word.

sentences.zh: 當是時，偽天王洪秀全僭號踞金陵，偽忠王李秀成等犯蘇、滬，偽侍王李世賢等陷浙杭，偽輔王楊輔清等屯寧國，偽康王汪海洋窺江西，偽英王陳玉成屯廬州，捻首苗霈霖出入潁、壽，與玉成合，圖竄山東、河南，眾皆號數十萬。

translations.literal: At that time the false Heavenly King Hong Xiuquan held Nanjing in regal style; the false Loyal King Li Xiucheng and others attacked Suzhou and Shanghai; the false Attendant King Li Shixian and others took Hangzhou in Zhejiang; the false Assistant King Yang Fuqing and others held Ningguo; the false Prince of Kang Wang Haiyang watched Jiangxi; the false King of Ying Chen Yucheng held Luzhou; Nian leader Miao Peilin ranged between Ying and Shou and joined Yucheng, plotting to flee into Shandong and Henan—all claiming hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan held Nanjing as Heavenly King; Li Xiucheng struck Suzhou and Shanghai; Li Shixian held Hangzhou; Yang Fuqing held Ningguo; Wang Haiyang menaced Jiangxi; Chen Yucheng held Luzhou; Miao Peilin’s Nian bands linked with Yucheng toward Shandong and Henan—each host claimed hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 國籓與國荃策進取，國荃曰：「急搗金陵，則寇必以全力護巢穴，而後蘇、杭可圖也。

translations.literal: Guofan and Guoquan planned the advance; Guoquan said: "Strike Nanjing in haste and the rebels must defend their nest with full strength—then Suzhou and Hangzhou can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Father and brother plotted the advance; Guoquan said: "Hit Nanjing hard and the enemy must guard their lair—then Suzhou and Hangzhou can follow.

sentences.zh: 」國籓然之。

translations.literal: " Guofan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Guofan agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃以江寧事付國荃，以浙江事付宗棠，而以江蘇事付李鴻章。

translations.literal: He entrusted Jiangning affairs to Guoquan, Zhejiang to Zongtang, and Jiangsu to Li Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Nanjing to Guoquan, Zhejiang to Zuo Zongtang, and Jiangsu to Li Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 鴻章故出國籓門，以編修為幕僚，改道員，至是令從淮上募勇八千，選良將付之，號「淮軍」。

translations.literal: Hongzhang had been Guofan’s student, served him as reviser on staff, became a circuit intendant, and now was ordered to raise eight thousand braves on the Huai, with good generals—called the "Huai Army."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang, once his pupil and staff reviser, now raised eight thousand Huai braves under picked generals—the Huai Army.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，拜協辦大學士，督諸軍進討。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was made Grand Secretariat Associate and directed all armies in the advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Tongzhi year he became Grand Secretariat Associate and directed the general advance.

sentences.zh: 於是國荃有搗金陵之師，鴻章有徵蘇、滬之師，載福、玉麟有肅清下游之師；

translations.literal: Thus Guoquan had the army to storm Nanjing, Hongzhang the army to recover Suzhou and Shanghai, Zaifu and Yulin the army to clear the lower river;
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan besieged Nanjing, Hongzhang recovered Suzhou and Shanghai, Zaifu and Peng Yulin cleared the lower Yangtze;

sentences.zh: 大江以北，多隆阿有取廬州之師，續宜有援潁州之師；

translations.literal: north of the great river, Duo Long’a had the army to take Luzhou and Xuyi the army to aid Yingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: north of the river Duo Long’a marched on Luzhou and Li Xuyi relieved Yingzhou;

sentences.zh: 大江以南，鮑超有攻寧國之師，運蘭有防剿徽州之師，宗棠有規復全浙之師：十道並出，皆受成於國籓。

translations.literal: south of the great river, Bao Chao attacked Ningguo, Yunlan guarded and fought at Huizhou, Zongtang aimed to recover all Zhejiang—ten columns at once, all under Guofan’s command.
translations.idiomatic: south of it Bao Chao struck Ningguo, Zhang Yunlan held Huizhou, Zuo Zongtang reconquered Zhejiang—ten armies at once, all answering to Guofan.

sentences.zh: 賊之都金陵也，堅築壕壘，餉械足，猝不可拔。

translations.literal: When the rebels made Nanjing their capital they built strong ramparts, with ample stores and arms, and it could not be taken in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing they had built deep walls and ample stores; the city could not be rushed.

sentences.zh: 疾疫大作，將士死亡山積，幾不能軍。

translations.literal: Epidemic disease broke out; officers and men died in heaps, and the army was nearly unable to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Plague killed men in heaps until the army could hardly stand.

sentences.zh: 國籓自以德薄，請簡大臣馳赴軍，俾分己責，上優詔慰勉之，謂：「天災流行，豈卿一人之咎？

translations.literal: Guofan, thinking his virtue thin, asked that a senior minister be sent to the army to share his burden; the emperor answered with an excellent edict of comfort, saying: "Epidemic disaster spreads—how is that your fault alone?
translations.idiomatic: Feeling unworthy, he asked for a senior minister to share command; the emperor comforted him: "Plague is Heaven’s doing—how is it yours alone?

sentences.zh: 意者朝廷政多缺失，我君臣當勉圖禳救，為民請命。

translations.literal: Perhaps court policy has many flaws—we ruler and ministers should strive to avert it and plead for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps the court has erred—we should pray for the people and mend policy.

sentences.zh: 且環顧中外，才力、氣量無逾卿者！

translations.literal: And looking within and without, in talent and breadth none surpasses you!
translations.idiomatic: Look around—in talent and force of character none matches you!

sentences.zh: 時勢艱難，無稍懈也。

translations.literal: The times are hard—do not slacken in the least.
translations.idiomatic: These times are hard—do not slacken.

sentences.zh: 」國籓讀詔感泣。

translations.literal: " Guofan read the edict and wept.
translations.idiomatic: " Reading the edict, Guofan wept.

sentences.zh: 時洪秀全被圍久，召李秀成蘇州，李世賢浙江，悉眾來援，號六十萬，圍雨花台軍。

translations.literal: At that time Hong Xiuquan, long besieged, summoned Li Xiucheng from Suzhou and Li Shixian from Zhejiang; all their hosts came to aid, claiming six hundred thousand, and besieged the army at Yuhuatai.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Xiuquan, long trapped, called Li Xiucheng from Suzhou and Li Shixian from Zhejiang; six hundred thousand men, they claimed, surrounded Yuhuatai.

sentences.zh: 國荃拒戰六十四日，解去。

translations.literal: Guoquan fought them off for sixty-four days until they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan held them sixty-four days until they broke off.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，水師克九洑洲，江寧城合圍。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year the navy took Jiufuzhou and Nanjing was fully invested.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year the fleet took Jiufuzhou and the ring around Nanjing closed.

sentences.zh: 十月，鴻章克蘇州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Hongzhang took Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Hongzhang took Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，宗棠克杭州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Zongtang took Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Zuo Zongtang took Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 國籓以江寧久不下，請鴻章來會師，未發，國荃攻益急，克之。

translations.literal: Guofan, because Nanjing was long untaken, asked Hongzhang to join the siege; before he set out, Guoquan pressed harder and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing still held; Guofan summoned Hongzhang to join the siege, but before he arrived Guoquan pressed harder and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 江寧平，天子褒功，加太子太傅，封一等毅勇侯，賞雙眼翎。

translations.literal: When Nanjing was pacified, the Son of Heaven rewarded merit: Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, enfeoffed as First-Class Marquis of Yiyong, with the reward of double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing pacified, the throne made him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, First-Class Marquis Yiyong, with double-eyed peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 開國以來，文臣封侯自是始。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the state, enfeoffment of a civil official as marquis began here.
translations.idiomatic: Never before had a civil official been enfeoffed marquis at the dynasty’s founding.

sentences.zh: 朝野稱賀，而國籓功成不居，粥粥如畏。

translations.literal: Court and country rejoiced, while Guofan, merit achieved, did not dwell on it and was timid as if in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The realm rejoiced, but Guofan, his work done, shrank from praise like a man afraid.

sentences.zh: 穆宗每簡督撫，輒密詢其人，未敢指缺疏薦，以謂疆臣既專征伐，不當更分黜陟之柄，外重內輕之漸，不可不防。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Muzong chose governors, he would secretly ask Guofan’s view; he dared not recommend by name in memorials, holding that frontier lords who already held military power should not also divide the power of appointment and dismissal—the tendency of outer weight and inner lightness must be guarded against.
translations.idiomatic: The young emperor secretly asked his view of every appointment; he would not name men in memorials, fearing that commanders with armies should not also control civil appointments—lest outer power outweigh the center.

sentences.zh: 初，官軍積習深，勝不讓，敗不救。

translations.literal: At first, deep habits had accumulated in the government army: in victory they would not yield merit, in defeat they would not rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops had long refused to share credit in victory or aid in defeat.

sentences.zh: 國籓練湘軍，謂必萬眾一心，乃可辦賊，故以忠誠倡天下。

translations.literal: Guofan trained the Xiang Army, saying only when ten thousand hearts are one can rebels be handled; therefore he raised loyalty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan built the Xiang Army on the belief that only united hearts could defeat the rebels, and preached loyalty across the land.

sentences.zh: 其後又謂淮上風氣勁，宜別立一軍。

translations.literal: Later he also said the Huai region’s spirit was vigorous and a separate army should be raised.
translations.idiomatic: Later he said the Huai country was hardy and deserved its own army.

sentences.zh: 湘勇利山徑，馳騁平原非所長，且用武十年，氣亦稍衰矣，故欲練淮士為湘勇之繼。

translations.literal: Xiang braves were skilled on mountain paths and not at home on open plains; after ten years of war their spirit had also somewhat declined; therefore he wished to train Huai men as successors to the Xiang braves.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang men excelled in hills, not on plains; after ten years their edge had dulled—he meant the Huai Army to succeed them.

sentences.zh: 至是東南大定，裁湘軍，進淮軍，而捻匪事起。

translations.literal: By then the southeast was largely settled; the Xiang Army was cut down and the Huai Army advanced, and Nian bandit troubles arose.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast was largely won; he disbanded the Xiang Army and raised the Huai, even as Nian rebels flared.

sentences.zh: 捻匪者，始於山東遊民相聚，其後剽掠光、固、潁、亳、淮、徐之間，捻紙燃脂，故謂之「捻」。

translations.literal: Nian bandits began with Shandong vagrants gathering; later they plundered between Guang, Gu, Ying, Bo, Huai, and Xu; they twisted paper to light grease, hence called "Nian."
translations.idiomatic: The Nian began as Shandong wanderers; they raided the Huai basin and lit twisted paper in grease—hence the name.

sentences.zh: 有眾數十萬，馬數万，蹂躪數千里，分合不常。

translations.literal: They had hundreds of thousands of men and tens of thousands of horses, trampling thousands of li, splitting and joining without fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: They fielded hundreds of thousands of men and myriads of horses, ravaging thousands of li, merging and splitting without pattern.

sentences.zh: 捻首四人，曰張總愚、任柱、牛洪、賴文光。

translations.literal: Four Nian chiefs: Zhang Zongyu, Ren Zhu, Niu Hong, and Lai Wenguang.
translations.idiomatic: Four chiefs led them: Zhang Zongyu, Ren Zhu, Niu Hong, and Lai Wenguang.

sentences.zh: 自洪寇、苗練嘗糾捻與官軍戰，益悉攻鬥，勝保、袁甲三不能禦。

translations.literal: Since Taiping and Miao militia rebels had often joined the Nian against government troops, they grew skilled in fighting; Sheng Bao and Yuan Jiasan could not check them.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping and Miao rebels had schooled them in battle; Sheng Bao and Yuan Jiasan could not hold them.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁征討數年，亦未能大創之。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen campaigned for years yet could not inflict a great wound.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen fought them for years without a decisive blow.

sentences.zh: 國籓聞僧軍輕騎追賊，一日夜三百餘裡，曰：「此於兵法，必蹶上將軍。

translations.literal: Guofan heard Seng’s army pursued with light cavalry three hundred-odd li in a day and night, and said: "In military law this must trip up the commander.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Seng’s light horse chased three hundred li in a day and night, Guofan said: "By the art of war that will break the general.

sentences.zh: 」未幾而王果戰歿曹州，上聞大驚，詔國籓速赴山東剿捻，節制直隸、山東、河南三省，而鴻章代為總督，廷旨日促出師。

translations.literal: " Before long the prince indeed died in battle at Caozhou; the emperor, greatly alarmed, ordered Guofan to hurry to Shandong to suppress the Nian, with command over Zhili, Shandong, and Henan; Hongzhang replaced him as governor-general, and court orders daily pressed him to march.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon the prince fell at Caozhou; the throne ordered Guofan to Shandong with command over three provinces while Hongzhang took his governorship, edicts pressing him daily.

sentences.zh: 國籓上言：「楚軍裁撤殆盡，今調劉松山一軍及劉銘傳淮勇尚不足。

translations.literal: Guofan submitted: "The Chu army is nearly all disbanded; now transferring Liu Songshan’s one army and Liu Mingchuan’s Huai braves is still insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "The Hunan army is almost gone; Liu Songshan and Liu Mingchuan’s Huai men are not enough.

sentences.zh: 當更募徐州勇，以楚軍之規模，開齊、兗之風氣；

translations.literal: More Xuzhou braves should be raised on the Chu model to open Qi and Yan spirit;
translations.idiomatic: We must raise Xuzhou braves on the Hunan pattern and stir Qi and Yan;

sentences.zh: 又增募馬隊及黃河水師，皆非旦夕可就。

translations.literal: cavalry and the Yellow River navy must also be added—not achievable in a day.
translations.idiomatic: cavalry and a Yellow River fleet cannot be ready overnight.

sentences.zh: 直隸宜自籌防兵，分守河岸，不宜令河南之兵兼顧河北。

translations.literal: Zhili should raise its own garrison troops to guard the riverbanks; Henan’s troops should not also cover Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili should guard its own banks; Henan should not cover Hebei too.

sentences.zh: 僧格林沁嘗週曆五省，臣不能也。

translations.literal: Sengge Rinchen once toured five provinces—I cannot.
translations.idiomatic: Sengge Rinchen once held five provinces—I cannot match that.

sentences.zh: 如以徐州為老營，則山東之兗、沂、曹、濟，河南之歸、陳，江甦之淮、徐、海，安徽之廬、鳳、潁、泗，此十三府州責之臣，而以其餘責各督撫。

translations.literal: If Xuzhou is made the base camp, then Yan, Yi, Cao, and Ji in Shandong, Gui and Chen in Henan, Huai, Xu, and Hai in Jiangsu, and Lu, Feng, Ying, and Si in Anhui—these thirteen prefectures are my charge, and the rest belong to each governor.
translations.idiomatic: With Xuzhou as base, thirteen prefectures in four provinces fall to me; the rest to local governors.

sentences.zh: 汛地有專屬，則軍務乃漸有歸宿。

translations.literal: When garrison zones have fixed ownership, military affairs gradually find their home.
translations.idiomatic: Fixed zones would give the war a center.

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「扼要駐軍臨淮關、周家口、濟寧、徐州，為四鎮。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Hold key points at Linhuaiguan, Zhoujiakou, Jining, and Xuzhou as four garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: " He proposed four garrisons: Linhuaiguan, Zhoujiakou, Jining, and Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 一處有急，三處往援。

translations.literal: When one place is urgent, three places go to aid.
translations.idiomatic: If one is attacked, three would relieve it.

sentences.zh: 今賊已成流寇，若賊流而我與之俱流，必致疲於奔命。

translations.literal: Now the rebels have become roving bandits; if we roam with them we must weary ourselves chasing.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy are roving bandits; to chase them everywhere is to exhaust ourselves.

sentences.zh: 故臣堅持初議，以有定之兵，制無定之寇，重迎剿，不重尾追。

translations.literal: Therefore I hold to my first plan: use fixed troops to control unfixed bandits, stressing interception, not tail-chasing.
translations.idiomatic: So I hold to fixed troops against roving enemies—block them, do not merely follow.

sentences.zh: 」然督師年餘，捻馳突如故。

translations.literal: " Yet after more than a year as commander, the Nian still raided as before.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet after a year in command the Nian still ranged freely.

sentences.zh: 將士皆謂不苦戰而苦奔逐，乃起張秋抵清江築長牆，憑運河御之，未成而捻竄襄、鄧間，因移而西，修沙河、賈魯河，開壕置守。

translations.literal: Officers and men all said the hardship was not fighting but running; they built a long wall from Zhangqiu to Qingjiang along the Grand Canal to block them; before it was finished the Nian fled into Xiang and Deng, so they shifted west, repaired the Sha and Jia rivers, and dug trenches to hold the line.
translations.idiomatic: Men complained they marched more than they fought; they walled the canal from Zhangqiu to Qingjiang; before it stood the Nian slipped into Xiang and Deng, so they moved west and trenched the Sha and Jia rivers.

sentences.zh: 分地甫定，而捻衝河南汛地，复突而東。

translations.literal: The zones had just been fixed when the Nian struck Henan garrison territory and again burst east.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly were the zones set when the Nian hit Henan’s line and surged east again.

sentences.zh: 時議頗咎國籓計迂闊，然亦無他術可制捻也。

translations.literal: At the time opinion often blamed Guofan’s plan as impractical, yet there was no other method to control the Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Critics called his strategy too slow, yet no other way could hold the Nian.

sentences.zh: 山東、河南民習見僧格林沁戰，皆怪國籓以督兵大臣安坐徐州，謗議盈路。

translations.literal: People of Shandong and Henan, accustomed to Sengge Rinchen’s fighting, all wondered at Guofan as commanding general sitting at ease in Xuzhou; slander filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong and Henan, used to Sengge Rinchen’s hard fighting, resented Guofan sitting in Xuzhou while slander filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 國籓在軍久，益慎用兵。

translations.literal: Guofan, long in the army, became ever more cautious in using troops.
translations.idiomatic: Years in the field made him ever more cautious about battle.

sentences.zh: 初立駐軍四鎮之議，次設扼守黃運河之策。

translations.literal: First he proposed the four garrisons; next the plan to hold the Yellow River and Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He began with four fixed garrisons, then the canal defense line.

sentences.zh: 既數為言路所劾，亦自以防河無效，朝廷方起用國荃，乃奏請鴻章以江督出駐徐州，與魯撫會辦東路；

translations.literal: Having been impeached several times by the censorate, and himself fearing the river defense ineffective, as the court was raising Guoquan, he memorialized asking Hongzhang as Jiangsu governor to encamp at Xuzhou and jointly handle the eastern route with the Shandong governor;
translations.idiomatic: Censors attacked him repeatedly; doubting the river line, and with Guoquan rising at court, he asked Hongzhang as Jiangsu governor to camp at Xuzhou with the Shandong governor on the east;

sentences.zh: 國荃以鄂撫出駐襄陽，與豫撫會辦西路：而自駐周家口策應之。

translations.literal: Guoquan as Hubei governor to encamp at Xiangyang and jointly handle the western route with the Henan governor: he himself would sit at Zhoujiakou to coordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan as Hubei governor to hold Xiangyang with the Henan governor on the west, while he coordinated from Zhoujiakou.

sentences.zh: 或又劾其驕妄，於是國籓念權位不可久處，益有憂讒畏譏之心矣。

translations.literal: Some again impeached him for arrogance; thus Guofan felt power and position could not be long held and grew fearful of slander.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh charges of arrogance made him feel power could not be held long, and he grew afraid of court intrigue.

sentences.zh: 匈病假數月，繼請開缺，以散員留軍效力；

translations.literal: Chest illness kept him on leave for months; he then asked to vacate his post and remain in the army as a private without rank;
translations.idiomatic: Chest trouble kept him on leave for months; he asked to resign his post yet stay with the army as a private;

sentences.zh: 又請削封爵：皆不許。

translations.literal: he also asked to strip his enfeoffment: none was granted.
translations.idiomatic: he begged to give up his marquisate—the court refused both.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，還任江南，而鴻章代督軍。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year he returned to duty in Jiangnan, and Hongzhang took command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth winter he returned to Jiangnan while Hongzhang took the field command.

sentences.zh: 時牛洪死，張總愚竄陝西，任柱、賴文光竄湖北，自是有東西捻之號。

translations.literal: At that time Niu Hong was dead; Zhang Zongyu fled into Shaanxi, Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang into Hubei—from this came the names Eastern and Western Nian.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hong was dead; Zhang Zongyu fled to Shaanxi, Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang to Hubei—the Eastern and Western Nian.

sentences.zh: 六年，就補大學士，留治所。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was confirmed as Grand Secretary while remaining at his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was confirmed Grand Secretary without leaving his post.

sentences.zh: 東捻由河南竄登、萊、青，李鴻章、劉長佑建議合四省兵力堵運河。

translations.literal: The Eastern Nian from Henan fled into Deng, Lai, and Qing; Li Hongzhang and Liu Changyou proposed uniting four provinces’ forces to block the canal.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Nian from Henan swept Deng, Lai, and Qing; Hongzhang and Liu Changyou proposed a four-province blockade of the canal.

sentences.zh: 賊復引而西，越膠、萊、河南入海州。

translations.literal: The rebels turned west again, crossed Jiao, Lai, and Henan, and entered the sea at Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: They turned west, crossed Jiao and Lai and Henan, and broke toward Haizhou on the sea.

sentences.zh: 官軍陣斬任柱，賴文光走死揚州。

translations.literal: Government troops cut down Ren Zhu in battle; Lai Wenguang fled and died at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhu was killed in battle; Lai Wenguang fled and died at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以東捻平，加國籓雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: With the Eastern Nian pacified, Guofan was given the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Nian subdued, Guofan received the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

sentences.zh: 西捻入陝後，為松山所敗。

translations.literal: After the Western Nian entered Shaanxi they were defeated by Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Nian, entering Shaanxi, were beaten by Liu Songshan.

sentences.zh: 乘堅冰渡河竄山西，入直隸，犯保定、天津。

translations.literal: They crossed the river on solid ice into Shanxi, entered Zhili, and attacked Baoding and Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the frozen Yellow River into Shanxi, entered Zhili, and threatened Baoding and Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 松山繞出賊前，破之於獻縣。

translations.literal: Songshan circled ahead of them and defeated them at Xian County.
translations.idiomatic: Songshan cut ahead and broke them at Xian County.

sentences.zh: 諸帥勤王師大至，賊越運河竄東昌、武定。

translations.literal: All the generals’ relief armies arrived in force; the rebels crossed the canal and fled to Dongchang and Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: Relief armies gathered; the Nian crossed the canal toward Dongchang and Wuding.

sentences.zh: 鴻章移師德州，河水盛漲，扼河以困之。

translations.literal: Hongzhang moved his army to Dezhou; the river was in flood and he held the line to trap them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang shifted to Dezhou, used high water to pen them in.

sentences.zh: 國籓遣黃翼升領水師助剿，大破賊於荏平。

translations.literal: Guofan sent Huang Yisheng to lead the navy in aid; they routed the rebels at Renping.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan sent Huang Yisheng’s fleet; the enemy was shattered at Renping.

sentences.zh: 張總愚赴水死，而西捻平。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongyu went to his death in the water, and the Western Nian were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongyu drowned; the Western Nian were gone.

sentences.zh: 凡防河之策，皆國籓本謀也。

translations.literal: All the river-defense plans were originally Guofan’s design.
translations.idiomatic: Every canal defense had been Guofan’s idea.

sentences.zh: 是年授武英殿大學士，調直隸總督。

translations.literal: That year he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory and transferred to Governor-General of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: That year he entered the Hall of Military Glory and became governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 國籓為政務持大體，規全勢。

translations.literal: In governing, Guofan held to the larger pattern and planned for the whole situation.
translations.idiomatic: In civil rule he held to large patterns and the whole strategic picture.

sentences.zh: 其策西事，議先清隴寇而後出關；

translations.literal: On western affairs he argued first to clear Long bandits then go beyond the passes;
translations.idiomatic: On the northwest he urged clearing Longzhou bandits before marching beyond the passes;

sentences.zh: 籌滇、黔，議以蜀、湘二省為根本。

translations.literal: on Yunnan and Guizhou he planned with Sichuan and Hunan as the root.
translations.idiomatic: on Yunnan and Guizhou he made Sichuan and Hunan the base.

sentences.zh: 皆初立一議，後數年卒如其說。

translations.literal: Each was first a single proposal, and years later events ended as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Each began as a single memorial—and years later events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 自西人入中國，交涉事日繁。

translations.literal: Since Westerners entered China, foreign affairs grew daily more complex.
translations.idiomatic: After Westerners entered China, foreign affairs multiplied daily.

sentences.zh: 金陵未下，俄、美、英、法皆請以兵助，國籓婉拒之。

translations.literal: Before Nanjing fell, Russia, America, Britain, and France all asked to aid with troops; Guofan politely refused.
translations.idiomatic: Before Nanjing fell, Russia, America, Britain, and France offered troops; Guofan declined politely.

sentences.zh: 及廷議購機輪，置船械，則力贊其成，復建議選學童習藝歐洲。

translations.literal: When the court debated buying steam engines and setting up ships and arms, he strongly urged success and again proposed selecting schoolboys to learn crafts in Europe.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated steamships and arsenals, he urged them on and proposed sending boys to learn crafts in Europe.

sentences.zh: 每定約章，輒詔問可許不可許，國籓以為爭彼我之虛儀者可許，其奪吾民生計者勿許也。

translations.literal: Whenever treaties were fixed the throne would ask what might be granted; Guofan held that empty ceremony with them could be granted, but what seized the livelihood of our people could not.
translations.idiomatic: On each treaty the throne asked what to concede; he would yield empty ceremony but never what stole the people’s livelihood.

sentences.zh: 既至直隸，以練兵、飭吏、治河三端為要務，次第興革，設清訟局、禮賢館，政教大行。

translations.literal: Once in Zhili he made training troops, correcting officials, and managing rivers the three essentials, reforming step by step, establishing bureaus for clearing lawsuits and honoring worthies—government and teaching flourished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhili he made training troops, disciplining officials, and river work his three tasks, reformed in order, opened bureaus for lawsuits and honoring talent—and rule flourished.

sentences.zh: 九年四月，天津民擊殺法領事豐大業，毀教堂，傷教民數十人。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the ninth year Tianjin people killed the French consul Fontanier, destroyed churches, and wounded dozens of Christians.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year’s fourth month Tianjin people killed the French consul Fontanier, wrecked churches, and wounded dozens of Christians.

sentences.zh: 通商大臣崇厚議嚴懲之，民不服。

translations.literal: Trade Commissioner Chonghou proposed severe punishment; the people would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Trade Commissioner Chonghou wanted harsh punishment; the people rebelled at the idea.

sentences.zh: 國籓方病目，詔速赴津，乃務持平保和局，殺十七人，又遣戍府縣吏。

translations.literal: Guofan was ill in the eyes; ordered to hurry to Tianjin, he sought balance to preserve peace, executed seventeen men, and exiled prefectural and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Half blind, he was ordered to Tianjin; seeking peace he had seventeen executed and prefectural officials exiled.

sentences.zh: 國籓之初至也，津民謂必反崇厚所為，備兵以抗法。

translations.literal: When Guofan first arrived, Tianjin people thought he would reverse Chonghou and prepared troops to resist France.
translations.idiomatic: At first Tianjin expected him to defy Chonghou and armed against France.

sentences.zh: 然當是時，海內初定，湘軍已散遣，天津咫尺京畿，民、教相閧，此小事不足啟兵端，而津民爭怨之。

translations.literal: Yet at that time the realm was newly settled, the Xiang Army disbanded, Tianjin was a stone’s throw from the capital, and though people and missionaries clashed, this small affair was not worth opening war—yet Tianjin people resented him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was barely pacified, the Xiang Army gone, Tianjin lay under the capital’s shadow—a brawl not worth war, yet the city hated him the more.

sentences.zh: 平生故舊持高論者，日移書譙讓，省館至毀所署楹帖，而國籓深維中外兵勢強弱，和戰利害，惟自引咎，不一辯也。

translations.literal: Old friends who held high views daily sent letters of reproach; provincial lodges even tore down his couplets; yet Guofan weighed foreign and domestic strength, the gain and loss of war and peace, and only blamed himself, never arguing back.
translations.idiomatic: High-minded friends daily scolded him by letter; lodges tore down his plaques; weighing strength and peace, he blamed only himself and never replied.

sentences.zh: 丁日昌因上奏曰：「自古局外議論，不諒局中艱苦，一唱百和，亦足以熒上聽，撓大計。

translations.literal: Ding Richang therefore memorialized: "Since antiquity outsiders debate without understanding the hardship within the situation; one voice leads a hundred echoes, enough to dazzle the ruler’s ear and thwart great plans.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Richang wrote: "Outsiders never grasp the difficulty within the case; one cry becomes a chorus that dazzles the throne and wrecks policy.

sentences.zh: 卒之事勢決裂，國家受無窮之累，而局外不與其禍，反得力持清議之名，臣實痛之！

translations.literal: In the end when affairs rupture the state suffers endless trouble while outsiders share no disaster, yet gain the name of holding pure opinion—I am truly pained!
translations.idiomatic: When things break the state pays endlessly while critics pay nothing yet keep their reputation for pure opinion—I grieve at it!

sentences.zh: 國籓既負重謗，疾益劇，乃召鴻章治其獄，踰月事定，如初議。

translations.literal: Guofan, bearing heavy blame, grew more ill; the throne summoned Hongzhang to handle the case; in a month matters were settled as at first proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Weighed down by blame and illness, he yielded the case to Hongzhang; within a month it ended as first planned.

sentences.zh: 會兩江缺出，遂調補江南，而以鴻章督直隸。

translations.literal: When the Two Jiangs post fell vacant, he was transferred to Jiangnan and Hongzhang made governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: A Jiangnan vacancy opened; he was shifted south and Hongzhang took Zhili.

sentences.zh: 江南人聞其至，焚香以迎。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan people heard he was coming, they burned incense to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan burned incense to welcome his return.

sentences.zh: 以亂後經籍就熸，設官書局印行，校刊皆精審。

translations.literal: Classics had nearly perished in the disorders; he established an official publishing house to print them, and collation was all careful.
translations.idiomatic: War had nearly destroyed the classics; he founded an official press with careful editions.

sentences.zh: 禮聘名儒為書院山長，其幕府亦極一時之選，江南文化遂比隆盛時。

translations.literal: He invited famous scholars as academy heads; his staff too were the choice of the age—Jiangnan culture again rivaled its height.
translations.idiomatic: He hired great scholars to head academies and staffed his yamen with the day’s best—Jiangnan culture rose again.

sentences.zh: 國籓為人威重，美鬚髯，目三角有棱。

translations.literal: Guofan’s bearing was imposing; he had a fine beard and triangular eyes with sharp corners.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing, bearded, with sharp triangular eyes.

sentences.zh: 每對客，注視移時不語，見者竦然，退則記其優劣，無或爽者。

translations.literal: Facing guests he would gaze a long time without speaking; visitors were awed; after they left he would record their strengths and weaknesses without error.
translations.idiomatic: With guests he would stare in silence until they quailed; afterward he noted their strengths without a miss.

sentences.zh: 天性好文，治之終身不厭，有家法而不囿於一師。

translations.literal: By nature he loved literature and pursued it all his life without weariness, having family tradition yet not bound to one teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He loved letters to the end, with family learning but no single school.

sentences.zh: 其論學兼綜漢、宋，以謂先王治世之道，經緯萬端，一貫之以禮。

translations.literal: His learning combined Han and Song; he held that the way of the ancient kings in governing the world, with its myriad strands, was unified by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Han and Song learning, holding that the kings’ governance, in all its strands, was one in ritual.

sentences.zh: 惜秦蕙田五禮通考闕食貨，乃輯補鹽課、海運、錢法、河堤為六卷；

translations.literal: Regretting that Qin Huitian’s Comprehensive Examination of the Five Rites lacked food and goods, he compiled supplements on the salt tax, sea transport, currency, and river works in six scrolls;
translations.idiomatic: Finding Qin Huitian’s Five Rites incomplete on economy, he added six scrolls on salt, sea transport, coinage, and rivers;

sentences.zh: 又慨古禮殘闕無軍禮，軍禮要自有專篇，如戚敬元所紀者。

translations.literal: he also grieved that ancient ritual was damaged and military ritual missing, holding it should have its own section, as Qi Jingyuan recorded.
translations.idiomatic: he lamented lost ancient rite and missing military ritual, which deserved its own section as Qi Jingyuan had shown.

sentences.zh: 論者謂國籓所訂營制、營規，其於軍禮庶幾近之。

translations.literal: Critics said the camp regulations Guofan drew up were perhaps close to military ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said his camp rules nearly embodied military ritual.

sentences.zh: 晚年頗以清靜化民，俸入悉以養士。

translations.literal: In later years he sought to transform the people through quietude and spent his salary entirely on nurturing scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he sought quiet to transform the people and spent his salary on scholars.

sentences.zh: 老儒宿學，群歸依之。

translations.literal: Old scholars and established learning all gathered to him.
translations.idiomatic: Veteran scholars flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 尤知人，善任使，所成就薦拔者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: He especially knew men and was good at employing them; those he advanced and raised cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: He knew men and employed them well beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 一見輒品目其材，悉當。

translations.literal: At one meeting he would size up their talent, and it always proved right.
translations.idiomatic: One meeting sufficed to judge a man—and he was never wrong.

sentences.zh: 時舉先世耕讀之訓，教誡其家。

translations.literal: He often cited his forebears’ teaching of farming and reading to admonish his family.
translations.idiomatic: He often preached his family’s farming-and-reading tradition to his kin.

sentences.zh: 遇將卒僚吏若子弟然，故雖嚴憚之，而樂為之用。

translations.literal: He treated officers and clerks like sons and nephews; though they feared him, they were glad to serve.
translations.idiomatic: He treated officers and clerks like kin; they feared him yet served gladly.

sentences.zh: 居江南久，功德最盛。

translations.literal: Long in Jiangnan, his merit and virtue were greatest there.
translations.idiomatic: His longest service and greatest merit lay in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 論曰：國籓事功本於學問，善以禮運。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Guofan’s achievements were rooted in learning; he was skilled in moving the realm by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Guofan’s feats grew from scholarship; he ruled through ritual.

sentences.zh: 公誠之心，尤足格眾。

translations.literal: His heart of utmost sincerity was especially able to move the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: His utterly sincere heart especially won men’s hearts.

sentences.zh: 其治軍行政，務求蹈實。

translations.literal: In governing the army and administration he strove for what was solid and real.
translations.idiomatic: In army and state he sought what was solid and real.

sentences.zh: 凡規畫天下事，久無不驗，世皆稱之，至謂漢之諸葛亮、唐之裴度、明之王守仁，殆無以過，何其盛歟！

translations.literal: Whatever he planned for the realm, in time none failed to prove true; the age all praised him, even saying that among Han’s Zhuge Liang, Tang’s Pei Du, and Ming’s Wang Shouren, perhaps none surpassed him—how grand!
translations.idiomatic: His plans for the empire proved true in time; men compared him to Zhuge Liang, Pei Du, and Wang Yangming—perhaps unequaled—such was his glory!

sentences.zh: 國籓又嘗取古今聖哲三十三人，畫像贊記，以為師資，其平生志學大端，具見於此。

translations.literal: Guofan also once took thirty-three sage and worthies of antiquity, made portraits and encomia, and took them as teachers; the main lines of his lifelong aspiration and learning are all seen here.
translations.idiomatic: He painted and praised thirty-three ancient sages as his teachers; his life’s aspiration shows in that act.

sentences.zh: 至功成名立，汲汲以薦舉人才為己任，疆臣閫帥，幾遍海內。

translations.literal: When merit was achieved and fame established, he urgently took recommending talent as his duty; frontier lords and commanders spread nearly across the seas.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of fame he made recommending talent his duty; his men commanded nearly every frontier.

sentences.zh: 以人事君，皆能不負所知。

translations.literal: Serving the ruler through men, all were able not to fail what they knew.
translations.idiomatic: He served the throne through men, and none betrayed his trust.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 中興以來，一人而已。

translations.literal: Since the restoration, there has been only this one man.
translations.idiomatic: Since the restoration, there has been only this one man.
